title: introduce session-handle + iterable adapters and batched retry profiles across SDKs
author: Maya Chen
description:
Context: multiple SDK consumers requested a lighter-weight session abstraction that is safe to pass between threads/tasks and that centralizes credential refresh + cancelation semantics. This PR introduces a small, explicit SessionHandle API and per-SDK Async/Sync iterable adapters that normalize backpressure and make retry profiles composable. Motivation: previous ad-hoc session objects leaked complexity (close/stop semantics differed by language), stream retries were duplicated, and containerized customers reported subtle reauth races under heavy load. Goals: (1) provide a minimal, language-idiomatic SessionHandle that implements lease semantics and a single 'Refresh' lifecycle; (2) expose AsyncIterable/Iterator adapters that unify chunking/backpressure across SDKs; (3) introduce 'batched' retry profiles tuned for streamed token workloads to reduce thundering retries and smooth burst behavior; (4) bump SDK package versions and add migration notes.

Summary of changes and checklist:
- SDK surface: python, typescript, go: introduce SessionHandle type (thread-safe lease token + Release/Keep methods)
- Python: add session_handle.py, SessionHandle context-manager ergonomics, AsyncIteratorAdapter for streaming responses
- TypeScript: add src/session/handle.ts, AsyncIterable adapter with for-await syntax, improve types for onPartial callbacks
- Go: add session/handle.go, lightweight Handle interface and Close semantics for goroutines
- Cross-sdk: add shared retry profile definitions (names: default, conservative, batched-stream), unify retry window config keys
- Tests: cross-language integration harness under devtools/sdktest that simulates reauth mid-stream and asserts no data duplication/loss
- Docs: add docs/sdk/session-handles.md with migration guide and example snippets
- Examples: add examples/streaming/reconnect.py and ts example demonstrating adapter usage
- Version bumps: python v1.9.0 -> v1.10.0, typescript v2.4.1 -> v2.5.0, go v0.9.7 -> v0.10.0

Migration notes (short):
- If you previously relied on SDK-specific session objects, switch to SessionHandle and call release/keep semantics as documented.
- Streaming bots that previously handled reauth should remove custom reauth loops and use the new batched retry profile for smoother retries.

Backwards compatibility: no breaking API removals; older session objects are shimmed to SessionHandle via a thin adapter for one release cycle.

Performance: microbenchmark shows 1-3% additional throughput for long-lived streams due to reduced reauth churn; memory overhead is negligible.

Security: auth windowing logic moved into SessionHandle to centralize KMS/HSM interactions.

Checklist:
- [x] API shape approved by SDK leads (Luca/Priya)
- [x] Cross-SDK unit tests added
- [x] Integration harness for reauth mid-stream
- [x] Docs + migration guide
- [x] Version bumps and publish scripts updated

CI notes: integration-sdks had one flaky run initially (intermittent mock clock drift), rerun stabilized and all checks passed.

Release process: squash-merge triggers the monorepo SDK publish pipeline (will create individual package releases for python/ts/go).

Related work: ENG-1429 (session lifecycle), ENG-1534 (retry profile tuning), SUP-331 (customer reauth incident).

Streaming: Add AsyncIterable/Iterator adapters to normalize backpressure and chunking across SDKs.
Retries: New 'batched' retry profile optimized for streamed token workloads to smooth bursts and reduce thundering retries.
Migration: Shims provided for one release; please consult docs/sdk/session-handles.md for migration steps.
